subject: Deployment compliance & hosting preference — next steps (BAA/SOC2 asks)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment compliance & hosting preference — next steps (BAA/SOC2 asks)

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements for HealthMesh's inference workloads.

Summary of call:
- Workload: PHI processing for appointment reminders and clinical summarization (subset of traffic).
- Primary concerns: HIPAA/BAA, SOC2 Type 2 evidence, encryption key control, audit windows for annual/quarterly audits.
- Preference mentioned: customer leans toward Private VPC, but open to Dedicated if BAA + customer-managed keys are available.

Our read (high level):
- Hosted API (with signed BAA) is the fastest route for non-PHI traffic.
- For PHI: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool + VPC peering) or Private (VPC/on-prem) are the options we should evaluate. Dedicated typically balances latency and operational overhead; Private VPC or on-prem gives max isolation and control.

Asks / action items from HealthMesh (please confirm or add):
1) Share your SOC2 Type 2 report (most recent period) or a summary of in-scope controls.
2) Confirm whether HealthMesh will require customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest.
3) Confirm expected audit window(s) (e.g., Q3 2026 external audit) and any evidence delivery deadlines.
4) Any additional compliance artifacts (pen test summary, infra segmentation diagrams).

What we'll deliver from Redwood by next Thursday (7/2):
- Redwood SOC2 summary doc (scoped for inference runtime + console). — attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf
- BAA template and simple execution options (DocuSign link if you prefer). — attached: redwood-baa-template.docx
- Short compare-and-ops checklist (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — attached: deployment-options-one-pager.pdf

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up to go over the artifact list and confirm whether Dedicated+VPC peering or Private VPC is required by your security team. I have availability Tue 6/29 09:00-11:00 PT or Wed 6/30 14:00-16:00 PT.

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Re: Deployment compliance & hosting preference — next steps (BAA/SOC2 asks)

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) SOC2: we'll need your SOC2 Type 2 report (most recent). If you can only share a summary and control mapping, that is fine for the initial evaluation but we'll request the full report under NDA later.
2) BAA: we require a signed BAA before any PHI is sent. We can execute electronically via DocuSign.
3) KMS: For PHI workloads we prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) in our cloud account. Need to confirm whether Redwood supports tenant KMS/HSM integration or if keys must be in Redwood-managed KMS.
4) Pen test / infra diagrams: please provide a pen test executive summary and network diagram that shows where inference runs (hosted control plane vs data plane).
5) Audit timing: we have a compliance gate the week of 7/20 — ideally we collect artifacts by 7/10 so internal reviewers can prepare.

Initial hosting preference: security team currently prefers Private VPC for PHI (full isolation). For latency-sensitive flows we might accept Dedicated with VPC peering if keys and audit logs are customer-visible.

I'll attach our internal compliance checklist in a separate email (security@ will send).

— Sara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment compliance & hosting preference — next steps (BAA/SOC2 asks)

Neha / Marissa — quick tech notes to include in the evidence packet and to share with HealthMesh security ahead of the call.

TL;DR: We support CMK for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted API, multi-tenant constraints mean CMK is not currently supported; we provide envelope encryption and token isolation.

Evidence / configuration items HealthMesh will likely ask for:
- SOC2 Type 2 report (we'll provide summary now, full under NDA).
- Penetration test executive summary and remediation tracker.
- Encryption: key management options (Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed CMK for Dedicated/Private). Include KMS integration docs and HSM support note.
- Networking: VPC peering diagrams, subnet mapping, security group ACLs, egress filtering.
- Audit logs: per-route token-level audit logs, KV cache access logs, and retention settings (we can export to your SIEM).
- Data residency: region control and physical location statements for Dedicated/Private.

Recommended hosting for PHI with moderate latency requirements: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering + CMK. If HealthMesh needs full physical isolation or has additional regulatory constraints, Private VPC/on-prem is the path.

I'll prepare a short one-page tech appendix for the call (will drop into the shared drive by 7/2).

—Karthik
